newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech economy not in crisis - bank governor.
newsitem.headline: Czech economy not in crisis - bank governor.

text.p: The Czech economy is not in crisis despite signs of a sharp slowdown and the central bank's (CNB) intervention to help the ailing crown, the bank's governor said in Saturday.

"I do not share the strong opinion that our economy is going through a deep crisis or that system errors in the process of (economic) transformation are being confirmed," Josef Tosovsky told the Czech daily Pravo.

He was referring to the CNB's sudden move on Friday to hike its Lombard last-resort lending rate to 50 percent from 14 percent in an attempt to shore up the sagging crown after several waves of direct intervention failed.
"(But) I do not expect any immediate strong impact on the economic growth," CNB board member Ludek Niedermayer told another daily, Mlada Fronta, Dnes on Saturday.
Whether such high rates would or would not have any negative impact on the economy would depend on how long the pressure on the crown persevered, he said.
"The speculations (with the crown) usually do not last too long, at most several days," Niedermayer told the daily.
He also said that the bank's measures had been strong enough and that the exchange rate could presumably be kept in the future.

The Czech crown has been heavily pressured over the past week as mainly foreign investors pushed the currency lower, hitting a record weak point of five percent on the depreciation side of its dollar/mark basket parity, prompting the CNB to intervene on the market for the first time in over a year.
The crown firmed immediately after the intervention and rose to about -2.6 percent to its parity rate from the previous -4.19 percent.
Analysts see the bank's move as correct but unmaintainable in the long run.
